Round Challah for Rosh Hashanah

Served at: Rosh Hashanah (Jewish New Year)

Makes 1 large round challah (Serves 8-10)Prep 30 min (plus 2-3 hours rising time)Cook 30-40 min

Challah is a rich, braided bread traditionally eaten on Shabbat and Jewish holidays. For Rosh Hashanah, the Jewish New Year, challah is often baked in a round shape to symbolize the cyclical nature of the year and a crown, representing God's sovereignty. This slightly sweet, golden loaf is a centerpiece of the festive meal, wishing everyone a sweet and complete year ahead.

Ingredients

  • 1 1/2 cups (360 ml) warm water (105-115°F / 40-46°C)
  • 2 1/4 teaspoons (7g) active dry yeast (one standard packet)
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) honey or granulated sugar, plus 1 teaspoon for yeast
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) vegetable oil, plus more for greasing
  • 2 large eggs, plus 1 egg for egg wash
  • 1 teaspoon (5g) salt
  • 6-6 1/2 cups (720-780g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
  • Optional: Poppy seeds or sesame seeds for topping

Method

  1. In a large bowl or the bowl of a stand mixer, combine the warm water, 1 teaspoon of honey or sugar, and yeast. Stir gently and let sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
  2. Add the remaining 1/2 cup honey or sugar, 1/2 cup vegetable oil, 2 eggs, and salt to the yeast mixture. Whisk until well combined.
  3. Gradually add the flour, 1 cup at a time, mixing with a wooden spoon or dough hook until a shaggy dough forms. If using a stand mixer, switch to the dough hook.
  4. Knead the dough on a lightly floured surface or with the dough hook for 8-10 minutes, until it is smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky. Add more flour, 1 tablespoon at a time, if the dough is too sticky.
  5. Lightly grease a large bowl with vegetable oil. Place the dough in the bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5-2 hours, or until doubled in size.
  6. Gently punch down the risen dough to release the air. Turn it out onto a lightly floured surface and divide it into 3 equal pieces.
  7. Roll each piece into a long rope, about 18-20 inches (45-50 cm) long. To form a round challah, coil each rope into a spiral, starting from the center, and then arrange the three spirals next to each other, gently tucking the ends underneath to create a single round loaf. Alternatively, you can braid the three ropes and then coil the braid into a spiral.
  8. Carefully transfer the shaped challah to a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Cover loosely with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise again in a warm place for 45-60 minutes, or until noticeably puffy.
  9. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
  10. In a small bowl, whisk the remaining egg with 1 tablespoon of water to create an egg wash. Gently brush the top and sides of the challah with the egg wash. If desired, sprinkle with poppy seeds or sesame seeds.
  11. Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until the challah is deeply golden brown and sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom. If it starts browning too quickly, you can loosely tent it with aluminum foil.
  12. Remove from the oven and transfer the challah to a wire rack to cool completely before slicing and serving.

Tips

  • For an extra sweet challah traditional for Rosh Hashanah, you can increase the honey or sugar by 1/4 cup (60 ml).
  • Ensure your water is not too hot, as it can kill the yeast, or too cold, which will inhibit its activation.
  • Challah freezes beautifully. Once completely cooled, wrap it tightly in plastic wrap and then in foil. Thaw at room temperature and warm gently before serving.
